interview.answer: A keyword that lets you style a specific part of an element or insert generated content, such as ::before or ::first-line.

interview.q: What is the difference between ::before and ::after?
interview.answer: ::before inserts content before the element's own content; ::after inserts it after.

interview.q: What must ::before and ::after have to render?
interview.answer: A content property; without it the pseudo-element is not generated.
Yes, they generate inline boxes unless you change their display.
It targets the first formatted line of a block, with only a subset of properties allowed.
It targets the first letter or character of a block, often used for drop caps.
It styles the portion of text highlighted by the user.
It styles the placeholder text of an input or textarea.
It styles the marker box of a list item, such as the bullet or number.
It styles the backdrop behind a dialog or popover in the top layer.
It styles the button inside an input type=file control.
It styles WebVTT captions in video or audio elements.
It styles elements distributed into a slot in a shadow DOM.
It styles a part exposed by a shadow DOM component via the part attribute.
Legacy forms like :before and :first-line that browsers still support for backwards compatibility.

interview.q: Why use double colons for pseudo-elements?
interview.answer: To distinguish them from pseudo-classes, as the specification recommends.
Yes, with content: url(...), though it is better to use a real img for meaningful images.

interview.q: What is generated content used for?
interview.answer: Decorative icons, clearfix hacks, counters and quote marks without extra markup.
Automatic numbering managed with counter-reset, counter-increment and content: counter().

interview.q: How do you create a numbered list with counters?
interview.answer: Reset a counter on the parent, increment it on each item and display it with ::before and content.
It creates or resets a named counter to a starting value, usually 0.
It increases a named counter by a given amount, defaulting to 1.
Yes, by resetting a counter inside a child, creating independent numbering per section.
It inserts the value of an HTML attribute into generated content.
It inserts the opening quotation mark for the current language.
It inserts the closing quotation mark for the current language.
It increments the quote level without inserting a mark, useful for nested quotes.
It generates an empty pseudo-element, useful for decorative boxes or clearfix.
Using ::after with content: '' and display: block to clear floats after a container.

interview.q: Why is clearfix less needed now?
interview.answer: Flexbox and grid do not collapse floats the way block flow does.
Font, colour, background, word-spacing, letter-spacing, text-decoration, text-transform, line-height and text-shadow.
Float, font, colour, background, margin, padding, border, text-decoration and text-transform.
Only colour and background are widely supported; other properties are ignored for security and consistency.
A light grey, but it can be overridden with ::placeholder.

interview.q: What is the opacity of ::placeholder usually?
interview.answer: Often around 0.5 to 0.7 depending on the browser, so explicit styling is safer.
Colour, font, content and a few text properties; layout properties are not allowed.

interview.q: Can ::marker be replaced with an image?
interview.answer: Not directly; use list-style-image on the list or a ::before pseudo-element for full control.
Styling the dimmed background behind a modal dialog or fullscreen element.
A special rendering layer above all other content, used by dialogs, popovers and full-screen elements.
It targets the content box of a details element when open, in supporting browsers.
It styles text flagged by the browser's spell checker, in supporting browsers.
It styles text flagged by the browser's grammar checker, in supporting browsers.
It styles text highlighted by text fragments in the URL.
It styles the root of a view transition, used for page or element transitions.
They style the outgoing and incoming snapshots during a view transition.
